statements.impact_statement: CVE-2025-15079: for SCP and SFTP transfers with a known_hosts file set, libcurl could still accept a host that is absent from that file if libssh's global known_hosts file lists it. Only curl's libssh backend (lib/vssh/libssh.c) is affected; upstream fixed it in 8.18.0: https://curl.se/docs/CVE-2025-15079.html, https://github.com/curl/curl/commit/adca486c125d9a6d9565b9607a19dce803a8b479. Debian builds curl with libssh2 for its SSH backend, not libssh: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2025-15079. Unpacked all 51 binary packages published from the curl source in the DHI Debian repository: curl 8.14.1 in its three published Debian revisions, built from Debian's 8.14.1-2+deb13u5 and 8.14.1-2+deb13u7 sources, for amd64 and arm64, namely curl, libcurl4t64, libcurl3t64-gnutls, libcurl4-openssl-dev, libcurl4-gnutls-dev and libcurl4-doc, and the debug-symbol packages curl-dbgsym, libcurl4t64-dbgsym and libcurl3t64-gnutls-dbgsym. Their ELF files are the curl program and the libcurl.so.4.8.0 (OpenSSL) and libcurl-gnutls.so.4.8.0 (GnuTLS) shared libraries, each dynamically linked against the system libc.so.6, plus detached debug-information files in the debug-symbol packages. The development packages also ship the static archives libcurl.a and libcurl-gnutls.a, each with 179 members that are all libcurl's own object files. No package contains a PE or Mach-O file. Both libcurl shared libraries link libssh2.so.1; no ELF file links libssh.so.4. In each static archive the libssh object, compiled from lib/vssh/libssh.c, is empty (608 bytes on amd64, 808 bytes on arm64) and defines no symbols, while the SCP and SFTP handlers are in the libssh2 object. The libssh code the advisory describes is not compiled into any build.
